target_customer: Startup founders incorporating and issuing stock, and the attorneys who work with them
problem: Routine startup legal paperwork (incorporation, founder stock, bylaws, board consents) consumed lawyer hours and inflated bills, and generic online services left lawyers fixing mistakes.
business_model: Per-package fees for legal paperwork software ($99 incorporation and $299 post-incorporation at 2013 launch)

founders.name: Darby Wong
education: University of Washington, computer science major
founders.background_notes: Machine learning research at UW per YC page.

founders.name: Chris Field
education: Stanford University, electrical engineering and history
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2013) says he was a lead attorney for Heroku in its acquisition by Salesforce.

competitors.name: LegalZoom and other online law sites
competitors.what: Generic online legal document services for small businesses

technical_complexity.rationale: Document automation with legal templates; the value was legal expertise encoded into forms rather than hard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Trusted templates and attorney relationships plus YC endorsement and a habit of using Clerky across batches; but the content could be copied by law firms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Law firms and later Stripe Atlas (built with Cooley) addressed incorporation; Stripe acquired Clerky in August 2026.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2013) reported over 100 startups incorporated through Clerky in stealth across three YC batches; founders and lawyers wanted cheaper standardized paperwork.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and founder friendly; footer states it is a bonded legal document assistant, not a law firm.

branding.brand_signature: Default choice of YC companies for incorporation
branding.community_and_virality: Its site claims 20,000+ startups incorporated and shows customer logos; no merch or fan evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong trust inside the startup community through YC use, but I found no press about the brand itself or name story.

outcome_analysis: Two former Orrick startup attorneys built Clerky inside YC's Summer 2011 batch, used it in stealth with YC companies, launched publicly in 2013, and reported 20,000+ startups incorporated by the 2020s. Stripe announced the acquisition in late August 2026. The founders' legal domain insight and distribution through YC explain its niche position; funding was tiny or undisclosed so it looks capital efficient.
notes: TechCrunch says launch was March 2013 (the article text I read dated March 11, 2013), though used in stealth earlier. Seed was undisclosed; aggregators claim a $130,000 YC investment on 2011-09-01 (YC standard deal, not recorded as round) and totals from $130K to $6.1M, all unverified. Stripe acquisition date: Aug 26 or 27, 2026 per two outlets; terms undisclosed. The competitor list comes from the 2013 TechCrunch launch article, not a 2011 source. YC page lists founders; education and prior employers come from it.
